summary: Small patch adds classmethod-property handling in MethodDocumenter and PropertyDocumenter, and tests pass. However the PropertyDocumenter.can_document_member addition is logically redundant (its second disjunct is a subset of the existing inspect.isproperty check), signaling a confused/incomplete fix mechanism, plus formatting nits.

issues.description: In can_document_member, `inspect.isproperty(member) or (isinstance(member, property) and inspect.isclassmethod(member.fget))` is redundant: `isinstance(member, property)` already implies `inspect.isproperty(member)` (isproperty ends in `isinstance(obj, property)`), so the added disjunct is dead code and cannot be what actually enables documenting the member. Approach/mechanism is unclear and fragile.

Relies on `obj.fget`/`member.fget` being a classmethod, which matches `@property @classmethod` ordering; the reported bug is `@classmethod @property` (classmethod wrapping property). Whether the member Sphinx retrieves is actually a `property` instance with a classmethod fget is version/retrieval dependent (Python 3.9 returns the computed value), making correctness across the reported case questionable.
Trailing whitespace after `or` and awkward manual line continuation instead of parenthesized/black-style wrapping; inconsistent with repo formatting.
No comment explaining the non-obvious classmethod+property descriptor handling, which future maintainers will find cryptic.
